_comment: defaultMode is 'dontAsk' rather than 'auto'. That is the actual fix: under
'auto' every shell command was still routed through a classifier that
re-prompted on anything it judged destructive - taskkill, rm, background
sweeps - which is why a wildcard allow list alone did not stop the
interruptions. The giveaway was exact rules like Bash(python run_tests.py)
continuing to accumulate underneath an existing Bash(*).
The deny list still wins over allow, so real study history stays protected
against both shell and editor writes.
If prompts somehow persist, 'bypassPermissions' is the full-off switch. It
requires accepting a one-time confirmation dialog, and that dialog is
deliberately not pre-accepted here - it is your call to click, not mine.
To tighten again: set defaultMode back to 'auto', or to 'default' to be
